text: morning all. reminder that my growth acceleration memo went out to the ELT last month and it's on the agenda when the consultants kick off. key points stand: chain book up 38% in two years, best growth engine we have. proposal is double down on chain bids and get street pricing sharper, 4-6 points
consultants can study whatever they want but the market doesnt wait for a study
read it again this morning, the numbers are strong. chain is carrying basically all our growth since 2023
chain revenue is up, yes. gross profit is not. those are different sentences
the mix problem is eating us alive. chain is now 27% of revenue at 12 points of margin, it was 20% two years ago
margin follows scale priya. we get teh volume, we earn the vendor rebates, we densify the routes. seen it work for 24 years
we have had two years of that thesis in production. blended GM went 20.9 to 19.8. we added $29M of revenue and about half a million of gross profit. at what point does the theory meet the ledger
which is exactly why street price is the play. we are bleeding accounts out there. churn is running 19% and continental is handing out intro pricing all over the metro
the 19 is the lapse flag, not churn. marcus wrote an entire memo reconciling this in feb. real net revenue attrition is single digits. please, everyone, read the memo before quoting the dashboard
the dashboard is the system of record last i checked
:face_with_raised_eyebrow:
on the account side theres also a reactivation angle - 3,100 accounts in the CRM btw. thats a big base, even winning back a slice of the quiet ones is real revenue
how many of those 3,100 placed an order in the last 12 months tyler
its everything in the accounts object, i pulled it straight from CRM this morning. can slice it however
slice it by the status field and then lets talk

jumping in on the PL appendix in dale's memo since it got one paragraph :) private brands is the one lever where growth and margin point the same way. our PL marging is 620bps over branded equivalents in matched categories
we're at 9% of sales today. every point of penetration is roughly $4.8M shifting to the better margin
fwiw i pulled some benchmark numbers and peer private label penetration is like 10%, so at 9% were basically at market. not much upside there imo
which cohort was that tyler
the MDC benchmarking study, the 2025 one from karen osweiler's shop. i can send the pdf
send it please. i want to see the actual exhibit, that number is way below what i hear at the category conferences
:thumbsup: sending after standup
either way it doesnt change the strategy. customers buy brands they know, PL is a nice-to-have on the margin. the demand fight is won on price and coverage
street operators switch to our labels every week when the rep actually plates a sample dale. the fight is rep attention, not customer resistance
can we at least agree that nobody reprices the whole street book while H&V are mid-engagement. carolyn was explicit that the price thesis gets tested, not assumed
six weeks. then we move. every week we wait continental signs another one of our accounts
happy to build the repricing model in the meantime so we're ready day 1
build the contribution model first. by segment. gross margin minus delivery cost per the ops study. then we can argue about price with the right denominator
on it :saluting_face:
also flagging ~60 PL sample requests from the april food show still open in the follow-up queue. reps, please work your lists, those are warm
gwen's recap said $3.2M in pipeline off that show. the demand is out there team, we just have to go get it
